# Is it a case for LicenRoute?

LicenRoute solves **commercial access**: who can use a paid route, with which licence and up to what quota. It does
not replace the app's authentication or infrastructure protection.

| The developer says… | LicenRoute? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Make them pay to query /api/reports" | Yes | Full flow |
| "100 free queries per customer and then pay" | Yes (trial licence) | See free-trial.md; do not promise anonymous queries |
| "Licences for AI agents that read my data" | Yes | Full flow |
| "Only registered users should get in" | **No** | The framework's authentication (Passport, JWT, sessions…) |
| "Don't let them take my server down" / DDoS / bots | **No** | Proxy, CDN, WAF or server rate limiting |
| "Limit to 10 requests per minute, without charging" | Usually not | The framework's rate limiting; LicenRoute only if there are also licences |
| API in Fastify, NestJS, Django, Laravel… | **No (not yet)** | Explain it; manual integration is not supported |
| Already charges with another solution that works | No, unless they ask | Ask what they want to change |
| Routes that already require login | Maybe | A licence would be an **additional** commercial layer; do not remove the authentication |

If it is not clear, ask: "Do you want to charge for or license access to these routes, or only control who logs in?".
